newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS, Lufthansa in joint sales pact.
newsitem.headline: SAS, Lufthansa in joint sales pact.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) said on Monday it formed a joint surplus materials sales unit in co-operation with its German partner Lufthansa.
It said in the in-house Inside SAS magazine that the new unit, named Surplus Sales Alliance, was formed by merging SAS' Technitrade unit with Lufthansa Technik.
SAS said the unit sold plane components, electronic and mechanical items, spare parts and aviation equipment to carriers and their agents throughout the world.

"Interest in buying spare parts has been explosive. In two weeks in October we sold $100,000 worth of parts. When we are in full operation we should be able to sell $400,000 worth per month," Copenhagen-based SAS Technitrade chief Henning Joergensen said.
He said Surplus Sales Alliance planned to increase activities, opening offices in the Pacific area and China and using SAS Technitrade's U.S. office for joint sales of technical parts and equipment.
SAS and Lufthansa, which formed a strategic alliance on January 1, 1996, have code-sharing and aircraft maintenance agreements, with Lufthansa Technik now servicing SAS aircraft engines at Hamburg.
